title: Find the best allowed plan

blocks.text: The checks of the previous practice are the first half of this one: paste your `evaluate_plan` into `best.py` (the starter leaves it empty), or write the checks again. The director wants the plan itself: of every allowed plan, the most valuable one. Portfolios in this tool have at most 15 projects, so checking every subset is fast enough.

Write `best_plan(projects, budget)` in `best.py`. It returns `(value, plan)`, where `plan` is a `frozenset` of project ids, for the allowed plan with the highest total value. When two allowed plans have the same value, return the one that costs less. When no plan is allowed at all, return `None`.

cases.says: the returned plan is allowed and its value is its projects' total value
no allowed plan is worth more than the one returned
a must-do project with negative value is still in the best plan
of two plans with equal value, the cheaper one is returned
when the must-do projects alone exceed the budget, the answer is None

origin.section: Checking a Plan Is Cheap; Finding the Best One Is Not

concepts: the best plan is the most valuable feasible plan, found by checking every allowed plan, not by ranking projects one by one
